title: nomux extension manifest
description: The manifest of a nomux extension package: extension.toml.

api.description: The `[adapter]` table needs the extension API version 0.1.1: the requirement must be `^0.1.1` or later.

id.description: The identifier of the extension: two or more parts with `.` between them, for example `nomux.git`. A part starts with a lower-case letter and has only lower-case letters, digits and `-`.

name.description: The name of the extension for the user.

version.description: The version of the extension (Semantic Versioning 2.0.0).

api.description: The extension API versions that the extension can use, as a caret requirement: `^1`, `^1.2` or `^1.2.3`.

daemon.description: The daemon part: a process that the nomux daemon starts on the Host.

command.description: The program of the daemon part: a relative path in the package.

lazy.description: `true`: the host starts the daemon part only when a client needs it. `false`: the host starts it together with the daemon.

ui.description: The UI part: a WASM component that the client runs.

component.description: The WASM component of the UI part: a relative path in the package.

slots.description: The slots that the UI part fills, for example `sidebar.section` or `tab.kind:diff`.

adapter.description: The agent tools whose hook events the extension takes: the extension is the adapter of these tools.

tools.description: The names of the tools, for example `testtool`. A name starts with a lower-case letter and has only lower-case letters, digits and `-`.

permissions.description: The permissions that the extension asks for. The user approves them at installation.

fs.description: The directories that the extension reads and writes. An item is an absolute path, or it starts with `${worktree}`.

process.description: The programs that the extension starts. An item is a program name without a directory.

network.description: `true` if the extension opens network connections.

scopes.description: The scopes of host services that the extension uses: a service name, `:` and an access name, for example `sessions:read`.
